result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers respect the flat, square brand: radius is zero with a circle exception, depth comes from thick rules and a zero-blur offset, and motion stays minimal with reduced-motion handling. B wins because it gives complete paste-ready CSS, including the reduced-motion media query. It also explains why overlays need the offset, offers a no-shadow alternative, and states which properties may transition. A is nearly as good, but its elevation tokens are a little muddled (elevation-2 just aliases elevation-1) and its reduced-motion rule is described rather than written out. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers follow the brand closely: zero radius with a justified circle exception, depth from borders plus a zero-blur offset, minimal motion with reduced-motion handling, and an explicit list of what is left out. A edges ahead because it gives a complete paste-ready CSS block with a raw layer and a semantic layer, a clear table of what makes raised and overlay elements different, and a no-shadow alternative for overlays. B's `--elevation-2` simply aliases `--elevation-1`, with the offset in a separate token, which makes it a bit less tidy and less ready to paste.
